validated_results.title: Chemoprevention of rat prostate carcinogenesis by soy isoflavones and by Bowman-Birk inhibitor.
validated_results.reason: This is an experimental chemoprevention study of soy isoflavones in MNU-induced prostate carcinogenesis in Wistar-Unilever rats, with no human participants or human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Chemoprevention of rat prostate carcinogenesis by soy isoflavones and by Bowman-Birk inhibitor.
validated_results.reason: The soy isoflavone mixture was administered only to rats undergoing induced prostate carcinogenesis, so the evidence is exclusively preclinical.

validated_results.title: Chemoprevention of rat prostate carcinogenesis by soy isoflavones and by Bowman-Birk inhibitor.
validated_results.reason: Soy component effects on prostate carcinogenesis were assessed only in a rat model, providing no original human incidence evidence.

validated_results.title: A prospective study of iodine status, thyroid function, and prostate cancer risk: follow-up of the First National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
validated_results.reason: Prospective human cohort follow-up of NHANES I reporting hazard ratios for incident prostate cancer across tertiles of urinary iodine/creatinine ratio, an iodine status biomarker.

extraction.comparison_type: High versus low urinary iodine tertile
extraction.population: Men in the NHANES I Epidemiologic Follow-up Study

effect_size.excerpt: Relative to the group with low urinary iodine, the age-adjusted hazard ratio was higher (although marginally insignificant) in the moderate group, hazard ratio 1.33 (95% confidence interval 1.00-1.78), and significantly lower in the high group, 0.71 (0.51-0.99). Thyroid disease was associated with an increased prostate cancer risk, 2.34 (1.24-4.43).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Relative to the group with low urinary iodine, the age-adjusted hazard ratio was higher (although marginally insignificant) in the moderate group, hazard ratio 1.33 (95% confidence interval 1.00-1.78), and significantly lower in the high group, 0.71 (0.51-0.99).

comparison.excerpt: Relative to the group with low urinary iodine, the age-adjusted hazard ratio was higher (although marginally insignificant) in the moderate group

design.excerpt: We investigated iodine status and prostate cancer risk prospectively using data from the NHANES I Epidemiologic Follow-up Study.

timing.excerpt: A prospective study of iodine status, thyroid function, and prostate cancer risk

continent.excerpt: data from the NHANES I Epidemiologic Follow-up Study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Participants were stratified into tertiles according to the urinary iodine/creatinine ratio, as a marker of iodine exposure.

validated_results.title: Effect of nutritional supplement challenge in patients with isolated high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia.
validated_results.reason: Selenium was given only within a combined selenium, vitamin E, and soy isoflavonoid supplement with no selenium-specific estimate for prostate cancer.

validated_results.title: Effect of nutritional supplement challenge in patients with isolated high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia.
validated_results.reason: Soy isoflavonoids were administered as part of a multi-nutrient supplementation challenge, so no soy-specific effect on prostate cancer detection can be separated.

validated_results.title: Effect of nutritional supplement challenge in patients with isolated high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia.
validated_results.reason: Vitamin E was inseparable from the combined selenium and soy isoflavonoid supplement, leaving no vitamin E-specific prostate cancer estimate.

validated_results.title: GSTM1 and GSTT1 polymorphisms and the risk of prostate cancer in a Caribbean population of African descent.
validated_results.reason: The study evaluates GSTM1 and GSTT1 genotype polymorphisms rather than any nutritional glutathione exposure, so the requested exposure is absent.

validated_results.title: Oral grape seed extract inhibits prostate tumor growth and progression in TRAMP mice.
validated_results.reason: Grape seed extract was administered by oral gavage exclusively to TRAMP transgenic mice, providing only preclinical evidence.

validated_results.title: Oral grape seed extract inhibits prostate tumor growth and progression in TRAMP mice.
validated_results.reason: The grape-derived exposure was tested only in a transgenic mouse prostate cancer model with no human participants.

validated_results.title: Isoflavone-rich soy protein isolate suppresses androgen receptor expression without altering estrogen receptor-beta expression or serum hormonal profiles in men at high risk of prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: Outcomes were circulating hormone concentrations and prostate androgen/estrogen receptor expression, with no assessment of incident prostate cancer.

validated_results.title: (n-6) PUFA increase and dairy foods decrease prostate cancer risk in heavy smokers.
validated_results.reason: Prospective CARET cohort analysis reporting a multivariate-adjusted hazard ratio for incident aggressive prostate cancer comparing higher with lower dairy food intake.

extraction.comparison_type: Higher versus lower dairy intake, aggressive prostate cancer
extraction.population: 12,025 men (heavy smokers) in the Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial (CARET)

sample_size.excerpt: This study investigates associations of dietary fat, meat, and dairy foods with prostate cancer risk among 12,025 men in the Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial (CARET). After 11 y of follow-up, 890 incident prostate cancers were reported and confirmed.

cases.excerpt: After 11 y of follow-up, 890 incident prostate cancers were reported and confirmed.

effect_size.excerpt: Red meat was not associated with total or aggressive prostate cancer. However, higher dairy intake had a statistically significant reduced risk of aggressive prostate cancer than lower dairy intake (HR = 0.59, 95% CI = 0.40-0.85).

confidence_interval.excerpt: However, higher dairy intake had a statistically significant reduced risk of aggressive prostate cancer than lower dairy intake (HR = 0.59, 95% CI = 0.40-0.85).

design.excerpt: Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate multivariate-adjusted hazard ratios (HR) of intake of fat and fat-related foods (meat and dairy) with prostate cancer incidence.

timing.excerpt: After 11 y of follow-up, 890 incident prostate cancers were reported and confirmed.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Diet was assessed by a biannual FFQ.

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: p_value
